scenes.title: Your API as a reusable piece

sentences.text: A custom connector is like a custom adapter for an odd plug.
You describe your API once, and then the agent, Power Apps, and Power Automate use it without repeating work.
One description of the A P I serves all those places and saves a lot of effort.
You build it in Power Apps or Power Automate, from an Open A P I file, a Postman collection, or from scratch.
You choose the authentication: no authentication, Basic, A P I key, or OAuth two point zero.
You can also add code in C sharp.
In Copilot Studio you use Add a tool and choose Custom connector.
You need a connection with your credentials.
And to move it between environments with solutions, you use connection references.
Think of the connection as the saved key, and the connection reference as a label that points to the right key in each environment.
Power Platform data policies also apply to custom connectors, and they can classify them by U R L pattern.
An administrator can allow or block your connector.
This way the security team decides whether your connector can be used in each environment.
If they ask you to use an internal A P I already described in Open A P I and reusable by Power Apps and Flows, the answer is custom connector.
The trap: forgetting that D L P also governs custom connectors.
Remember both points to answer with confidence on the exam.
